notes.summary: Audited new102: locally bounded real generated CLD Psh sections give middle-positive doubly closed ordinary multipliers through every sheafified ordinal, for all original fields, opens and current degrees. This proves separate-product positivity and an ordered recursion, not original P21.3 equality.
notes.detailedSummary: The locally bounded FINAL section forces each decreasing predecessor to be finite and locally bounded: it supplies lower bounds, and predecessor upper semicontinuity supplies upper bounds. A direct middle-cone coefficient-matrix argument validates locally bounded Borel order-zero multiplication without strongly-positive spanning. Fixed compact coefficient measures then give bounded convergence at successors; ordinary locality handles all intermediate sheafification and limit ranks. The result includes finite continuous generated Psh without reverse CPsh recognition, trivial valuation and singular/nonreduced spaces. Both signs generated Psh imply zero multiplier, but equal canonical Hessians of U,V do not supply that membership. No signed-relation preservation or analytic counterexample is proved.
notes.text:
Original P21.3 is unresolved; candidate=false. This is an unverified proof reconstruction of the supplied unreviewed new102 suggestion, with no novelty or priority claim.

Theorem. Let K be any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation; let X be good, separated, strict, boundaryless, pure of dimension n>=2; let W be any ordinary open. Let T be a middle-positive ordinary CLD (p,p) current, 0<=p<=n-1, with d'T=d''T=0. For every locally bounded real section f of generated CLD Psh(W), the ordinary Borel product fT is defined, and D(fT), D=d'd'', is middle-positive and doubly closed. All actual generic component multiplicities remain in the canonical calibration. The theorem includes possibly discontinuous locally bounded USC sections and all finite continuous generated-Psh potentials.

Exact primary premises, version and applicability. CLD means arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2. Its 8.1.1 defines the minimal ORDINARY sheaf generated by smooth positive-Hessian functions and decreasing sequential limits; 8.1.4 defines ordinary-local successor limits and ordinary-local earlier-rank membership at limits. Its 6.5.2 decomposes every compact symmetric test into two compact middle-positive tests; the analytic support scope explicitly includes almost-good spaces, so good suffices. Its 7.2.1--4 defines middle positivity and ordinary locality. Its 7.2.7(b) permits a middle-positive smooth factor against a middle-positive current. Its 7.2.8 and 7.2.11 give positive scalar coefficient Radon measures, compact for compact tests. Its 1.2.6--7 identifies the middle cone with signed positive-semidefinite exterior-power coefficient matrices; 7.1.1--3 gives chartwise C^0 continuity and finite smooth localization. The only part of 12.2.4 used is finite polyhedrality of a compact moment image, not its printed dimension assertion. The ordinary restriction, sheaf, smooth multiplier and differential identities are 7.1.6--7, 8.5.3--4 and 7.7.1--5. Applicability of this calculus to either valuation and every ordinary open is 11.1.7, 15.2.2--9 and 15.7.1--2. Canonical integration is positive and doubly closed; 16.6.3 retains generic lengths. These are external published premises, not independently re-proved foundations. The complete premise list and literal bodies/proofs are indexed 0--6 in premises.json and P21.3-primary-evidence.md. No CPsh recognition theorem is a premise.

Proof of Borel multiplication. For a compact symmetric complementary test eta write eta=eta1-eta2 with middle-positive compact tests. Define mu_eta=mu_eta1-mu_eta2 from T's positive coefficient measures. Independence of this decomposition follows because the measures agree on compact smooth scalars, hence by smooth density on compact continuous scalars, hence as Radon measures. The same argument gives linearity, compatibility with restriction, and support contained in supp eta. Set <fT,eta>=integral f dmu_eta; discard the antisymmetric test part by symmetry. This defines a linear symmetric functional for locally bounded Borel f.

To check ordinary current continuity, localize a fixed test family to a moment g:O->E using a nonnegative compact smooth scalar rho. Choose a compact analytic domain C inside O with supp rho in its interior. Its moment image has finitely many tangent faces. Put Theta=sum d'x_i wedge d''x_i in Euclidean coordinates. On each tangent face of dimension at least q, Theta^q is positive definite on the exterior power. The coefficient-matrix description gives, for a presented symmetric (q,q) test a, c||a||_(P,0)Theta^q +/- a >=0 on all faces, with c fixed for the finite presentation. Faces of smaller dimension give zero restrictions; for q=0 use Theta^0=1. Pull back and multiply by rho. Positivity gives signed measure bounds
  |mu_(rho g*a)| <= c||a||_(P,0) mu_(rho g*Theta^q).
Consequently
  |<fT,rho g*a>| <= c||f||_(supp rho)||a||_(P,0)<T,rho g*Theta^q>.
This is a fixed C^0 bound. Finite smooth localization proves order-zero continuity on every test family. Thus the product is an ordinary current even for discontinuous f; smooth multiplication agrees with the existing calculus. No strongly-positive spanning inference from the broader source 7.2.9 is used. Restriction follows by extending compact tests by zero and identifying their coefficient measures on smooth scalars.

Proof at every sheafified ordinal. Define P_0 by smooth positive Hessians, P_(xi+1) by ordinary-local decreasing sequences from P_xi, and P_lambda by ordinary-local earlier-stage membership. All stages are USC: decreasing infima satisfy {inf_j f_j<a}=union_j{f_j<a}; USC is local at limits. Finite USC sections are Borel. The stages are increasing. The set of all (ordinary open, ambient section) pairs bounds the length of a strictly increasing chain, so a stage equals its successor. It then remains stationary, is closed under decreasing sequences on each open, contains the generators and is a sheaf. Minimality proves that it is precisely Psh. No locally-integrable restriction is added to the definition.

Induct simultaneously over all ordinary opens and allowed T for locally bounded real sections. At rank zero, D(fT)=Df wedge T by both closedness equations, and the positive-factor rule proves middle positivity. At a successor, on one ordinary neighbourhood N write f_j in P_xi(N), decreasing to the bounded final f. Because f_j>=f, no predecessor is -infinity; +infinity is excluded by the ambient function sheaf. The final f supplies local lower bounds. Finite USC of each f_j supplies local upper bounds. Thus EACH predecessor is locally bounded, and induction applies without asserting its continuity or a global smooth presentation.

Fix a compact symmetric smooth test alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1). Decompose Dalpha=eta1-eta2 into compact positive complementary tests of the fixed T|N, with finite positive coefficient measures mu1,mu2. On their compact support union there are finite constants a,b, independent of j, such that a<=f<=f_j<=f_1<=b. Lower bounds follow by finite-cover local boundedness of f; upper bounds by USC and compactness of f1. The Borel nonnegative g_j=f_j-f decrease to zero and are bounded by b-a. For epsilon>0, E_j={g_j>=epsilon} decrease to empty, so finite measure gives mu_i(E_j)->0. Hence integral g_j dmu_i <=epsilon mu_i(C)+(b-a)mu_i(E_j) tends to zero after epsilon->0. Therefore
  <D(f_jT),alpha> = integral f_j dmu1 - integral f_j dmu2
       -> integral f dmu1 - integral f dmu2 = <D(fT),alpha>.
Every positive alpha has a nonnegative left side by induction. Symmetry of fT and DJ=JD gives symmetry of the limit Hessian. Restriction compatibility and ordinary locality give positivity on W. Intermediate predecessor covers are handled by the preceding inductive theorem, with no potential gluing and no countable intersection of neighbourhoods. At a limit, the final locally bounded f belongs near each point to one earlier stage; induction there and ordinary locality conclude. Stationarity proves the theorem for generated Psh. Finally d'DS=0 and d''DS=-d'(d'')^2S=0 for any current S, proving double closedness. For p=n-1 the alpha tests are scalars, so this endpoint is included.

Consequences and limits. Applying the theorem successively defines the ORDERED positive doubly closed recursion T_0=T, T_k=D(f_kT_(k-1)) for locally bounded generated Psh f_k and k<=n-p. No commutativity or curvature-independence is asserted. If h and -h are both locally bounded generated Psh, both D(hT) and its negative are middle-positive. Compact symmetric-test decomposition and symmetry show the current is zero. For the original h=U-V, equal canonical Hessians have not produced these two generating memberships. The theorem gives positivity of D(UT) and D(VT) separately, not equality. An induction on separate decreasing representations supplies no predecessor curvature relation to pass to the limit. It also supplies no regularization of T or restriction of an ambient Hessian equation to a curve.

notes.summary: Analytic diagnostic from GR Shilov geometry: on any fixed compact affinoid over any complete field, every linear subspace of classical pluriharmonic functions is closed under pointwise convergent nets; convergence is uniform. This cannot recognize an arbitrary P21.3 pair difference or establish multiplier equality.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite Shilov evaluation is injective on the classical pluriharmonic space and determines the supremum norm. The evaluation image of any linear subspace is closed in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, so a net converging pointwise to a finite function converges uniformly to an element of that same subspace, without assuming continuity of the limit. In particular enlarging smooth classical pluriharmonic approximation from sequences to nets on one fixed compact affinoid adds no nonsmooth limits. The proof uses GR v2 7.2--7.3 with their exact field scope. GR 7.8 still requires a genuine strictly semistable model and already classical pluriharmonic input. No two-sign recognition, model existence, ordinary-current descent or analytic counterexample is obtained.
notes.text:
Theorem. Let A be a compact K-affinoid space over any complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field. Let PH(A) mean CLASSICAL pluriharmonic functions, and let L be any real linear subspace of PH(A). Every net h_a in L converging pointwise on A to a finite real function h has h in L and converges uniformly on A. Continuity of the limit is a conclusion, not a hypothesis. This also holds on a compact analytic space with a finite affinoid-domain cover, using the union of the finite Shilov boundaries.

Exact external analytic premise. GR means W. Gubler and J. Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2. Definition 7.1 requires both signs to be classically psh, and 7.2 gives continuity and a real vector space. Proposition 7.3 states that on a K-affinoid with Shilov boundary Gamma, every already classical pluriharmonic function attains its global maximum and minimum on Gamma and evaluation PH(A)->R^Gamma is injective. The paper's field convention permits trivial valuation; 7.3 imposes no goodness, strictness, smoothness or reducedness restriction on the affinoid. The full relevant statement and printed proof, plus its primary maximum-principle antecedent 6.4 and the 7.1--7.8 scope, were read through the public primary PDF browser and frozen as literal browser-extracted units. This is an external published theorem, not an independently audited proof of all its cited foundations. Its provenance is premise index 7 in premises.json. Original GR PDF bytes were unavailable: only browser text hashes, not a PDF hash, are asserted.

Proof. E:PH(A)->R^Gamma is a linear injection. The maximum/minimum assertions imply ||v||_A=max_(x in Gamma)|v(x)| for all v in PH(A). The image E(L) is a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional R^Gamma and is closed: choose a basis, extend it to a full basis, and express the subspace as the common zero set of the remaining continuous coordinate functionals. Pointwise convergence of the original directed net on the FINITE set Gamma is convergence in R^Gamma, since a common upper index handles the finitely many coordinates for each tolerance. Its limit lies in E(L), so equals E(v) for one v in L. The exact norm identity gives ||h_a-v||_A=max_Gamma|h_a-v|->0. Uniqueness of pointwise limits gives h=v. No passage from the net to a sequence is made. For a finite affinoid-domain cover, the same argument applies to the union of the Shilov boundaries, and the supremum over the space is the maximum of its finitely many restricted suprema.

Approximation implication. L={v in PH(A):v ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth FORM Hessian} is a real linear subspace. Therefore every pointwise net limit of such functions on this SAME A is already in L. In the good strict CLD scope, smooth functions with zero smooth Hessian have both signs among the generated Psh generators; GR section 1.2's inclusion into classical psh makes them classically pluriharmonic. Thus replacing a sequence by a net of such fixed-affinoid harmonic approximants does not enlarge the closure. This observation is a diagnostic of the harmonic approximation route. It says nothing about approximants on shrinking domains or about arbitrary ordinary zero-current functions.

Research limitations. For actual P21.3 U,V, GR 1.2 recognizes each separately as classically psh but gives no subtraction closure. Equality D[U]=D[V] is an ordinary ambient-current relation and has not been shown to give both signs of U-V under the classical curve tests after every analytic field extension. GR 7.8's real-PL conclusion further requires a nontrivially valued field and an actual strictly semistable formal model of a good quasicompact strict domain. These assumptions are not obtained for arbitrary target germs; the source's skeleton interpolation cannot be invoked without them. The net theorem adds no new Bedford--Taylor range and constructs no admissible analytic counterexample. Nonsmooth residual-Picard real-PL examples remain in the already granted positive multiplier scope.

The concrete unproved sufficient analytic step is a valid construction, locally on one fixed ordinary neighbourhood, of BOTH U-V and V-U in the original generated Psh sheaf for every actual continuous equal-curvature generated-Psh pair. Another viable route would have to prove all-refinement-compatible positive doubly closed current regularization or signed-relation preservation directly. No such mechanism is proved here. No ambient Hessian restriction to curves, current ascent through a transcendental extension, arbitrary strong lift/product bridge or current-density theorem is assumed.
